questions.q: To apply a 'tint' (a lighter value) to a colour in a painting, an artist will typically mix the pure colour with what?
questions.explain: In painting terminology, adding white to a pure colour creates a lighter value known as a 'tint'. Adding black creates a 'shade'.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design

questions.q: In a drawing of a vase sitting on a table, the vase itself is considered the positive space. What does the empty area surrounding the vase represent?
questions.explain: Positive space refers to the main subject of an artwork, while negative space refers to the empty or open space around and between the main subjects.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: An artist draws a road getting narrower as it reaches the top of the paper to make it look like it stretches far away. Which element of design is being manipulated to create this illusion of depth?
questions.explain: By using linear perspective (making objects smaller as they recede), the artist is manipulating the element of Space to create the illusion of three-dimensional depth on a two-dimensional surface.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: By repeatedly placing thin lines very close together (a technique called hatching), an artist can make an area look significantly darker. In this application, 'Line' is being used to build up which other element?
questions.explain: Hatching and cross-hatching are line techniques used to create variations in lightness and darkness, thereby building up the element of Value (or Tone).
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: How can an artist realistically transform a flat 2D 'shape' (like a circle) into a 3D 'form' (like a sphere) on a flat sheet of paper?
options: By cutting out the shape with scissors
By applying varying values (shading) to mimic light and shadow
By outlining the shape multiple times with a thick black pen
By coloring the entire shape uniformly with a bright primary colour
questions.explain: The primary way to turn a 2D shape into a convincing 3D form on a flat surface is by applying value (shading). Highlights and shadows create the illusion of volume and depth.
